name: ainxt-vscode
description: AiNxt — governed AI coding agent for VS Code. A thin client over the AiNxt CLI (ACP); all policy/egress/exec guardrails and approvals are enforced by the agent.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Start chatting with AiNxt.
[Connect to AiNxt](command:acp.connectAgent)

acp.agents.description: The AiNxt agent configuration (spawns the governed AiNxt CLI over ACP). The ainxt.gatewayUrl, ainxt.model, ainxt.binaryPath, and ainxt.homeDir settings override the values here.

acp.autoApprovePermissions.description: Automatically approve agent permission requests. 'ask' always prompts (recommended). 'allowAll' approves everything without prompting — only use in trusted environments.

acp.defaultWorkingDirectory.description: Default working directory for agent sessions. Leave empty to use the current workspace folder. Can also be set via the AINXT_CWD environment variable.

acp.logTraffic.description: Log all ACP protocol traffic to the output channel. Off by default — enable only for debugging, as it logs all prompts and file contents.

ainxt.gatewayUrl.markdownDescription: Optional AiNxt Platform gateway URL, for teams that run the shared `ainxt-enterprise` service (auth, budgets, policy, audit). Leave empty to run the `ainxt` CLI standalone — it talks directly to whatever model you configure in `~/.ainxt/config.toml` or via an API key, with no gateway involved. Can also be set via the `AINXT_GATEWAY_URL` environment variable. Set by IT via machine or user settings for shared office-network gateways. Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace must not be able to redirect where credentials are sent.

ainxt.binaryPath.description: Full path to the ainxt CLI binary. Leave empty to use 'ainxt' from PATH. Can also be set via the AINXT_BINARY_PATH environment variable. Machine-scoped: it cannot be set by workspace settings, so opening an untrusted folder cannot redirect the agent to a different executable.

ainxt.homeDir.description: AiNxt home directory (where credentials.json lives). Leave empty to use the default (~/.ainxt). Can also be set via the AINXT_HOME environment variable. Useful when ainxt is installed in a non-standard location.

ainxt.model.description: Default model for AiNxt. Leave empty to use the agent's built-in default. Examples: claude-3-5-sonnet (Anthropic), gpt-4o (OpenAI), local:llama3:8b (Ollama). Can also be set via the -m flag in acp.agents args.

ainxt.allowInsecure.markdownDescription: Allow connecting to a plaintext **http://** or self-signed AiNxt gateway on an internal network. Off by default — enabling relaxes transport security (`AINXT_ALLOW_INSECURE=1`). Only enable for trusted office endpoints.

ainxt.autocomplete.markdownDescription:
Enable inline ghost-text autocomplete backed by the gateway's `/complete` endpoint. Off by default.

⚠️ **Privacy notice:** When enabled, up to 8,000 characters of the current file are sent to your configured gateway on each keystroke (debounced). Ensure your gateway is trusted and uses **HTTPS** for non-localhost connections. The extension does not control where the gateway forwards requests.

ainxt.registryUrl.description: URL of the ACP agent registry JSON. Leave empty to use the default public registry (cdn.agentclientprotocol.com). Set to an internal URL if your organisation hosts a private registry mirror. Must be https:// (or a loopback mirror); a plain http:// remote URL is ignored. Machine-scoped: it cannot be set by workspace settings, so opening an untrusted folder cannot redirect the registry fetch. Note: the registry URL receives your IP address when browsed.

scripts.build:webview: cd webview-ui && npm install && npm run build
scripts.copy:legal: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');for(const f of ['LICENSE','NOTICE','THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES']){const s=path.join(__dirname,'..',f);if(fs.existsSync(s))fs.copyFileSync(s,path.join(__dirname,f));else console.warn('missing '+f+' at repository root');}"
scripts.copy:profiles: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');const src=path.join(__dirname,'../config');const dst=path.join(__dirname,'config');if(!fs.existsSync(src)){console.log('no ../config in this tree; using the profiles already in vscode-acp/config/');process.exit(0)}if(!fs.existsSync(dst))fs.mkdirSync(dst,{recursive:true});fs.readdirSync(src).filter(f=>f.endsWith('.ainxtprofile.json')).forEach(f=>fs.copyFileSync(path.join(src,f),path.join(dst,f)));console.log('Profiles copied to vscode-acp/config/')"
scripts.package: npm run copy:profiles && npm run copy:legal && npm run build:webview && npm run package:ext
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run compile && npm run lint
scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run copy:profiles && npm run copy:legal && npm run build:webview && npm run package:ext

untrustedWorkspaces.description: AiNxt spawns the ainxt agent as a subprocess and lets it read and write workspace files and run terminal commands. That is not safe to enable for a workspace you have not trusted.
